terms.grammar: phrase: tegimentum, tegimentī n., with the genitive of ōs
terms.comment: Our description; no reference work has a word for a face mask. The thing is ancient: workers polishing minium tied loose bladders over their faces so as not to breathe the dust, faciem laxīs vēsīcīs inligant (Plin. NH 33.122, in Lewis & Short).
Classically the actor’s mask over the whole head; Levi–Bini give it for any mask. For a face mask it suggests a disguise.

phrases.latin: Ōris tegimentum indue; in medicīnam intrāmus.
phrases.english: Put your mask on; we’re going into the doctor’s.

sources: Lewis & Short: tegimentum · Lewis & Short: os · Lewis & Short: persona · Lewis & Short: vesica
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 40 (maschera).
